data.source_transplant: The double-exposure correlation interrogation of holographic PIV. The cross-correlation of two exposures of a particle field peaks at the displacement shared by all particles; the peak grows with the number of particles, while unmatched particle pairs form a flat background. Here it is computed with the HRR circular-correlation (bind/unbind) operator, and relative displacement is recovered from a superposed composite with the HRR inverse.

data.notes: No listed paper proposes sequence memory as pulsed mass-action binding with strand-exchange reactions under conservation. The closest items are linear-transformer/fast-weight equivalences (2310.16076), delta-rule and query-aware state updates (2606.08804), and Sinkhorn/optimal-transport attention (2605.08123). These share a key-value memory or a transport-style normalization but not the pulse recursion. The mass-action paper 1208.0874 covers persistence of mass-action kinetics, not memory. The card's cited sources W2989086808 and 1712.06281 do not appear in the search results, so they are not used as evidence. None of the found papers shows the central claim fails, and none tests the listed capabilities, so the known_disproven and prior_art_tested labels do not apply. The capability predictions, including the cross-ratio separation and the 4000-filler robustness, remain untested by any found work.
